senses.definition: To set the boundaries or limits of.

quotes.text: [God] hath determined the times before appointed.

senses.definition: To ascertain definitely; to figure out, find out, or conclude by analyzing, calculating, or investigating.

quotes.text: Whether modern, industrial man is less or more warlike than his hunter-gatherer ancestors is impossible to determine. The machine gun is so much more lethal than the bow and arrow that comparisons are meaningless.
quotes.reference: 2013 July 20, “Old soldiers?”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8845:

senses.definition: To fix the form or character of; to shape; to prescribe imperatively; to regulate; to settle.

quotes.text: The character of the soul is determined by the character of its God.
quotes.reference: 1741 July 8, Jonathan Edwards, Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God:

quotes.text: something divinely beautiful […] that at some time or other might influence or even determine her course of life

These dramas may appear purely internal but they are perhaps economically determined … when people think they are being so subtly inventive or creative they merely reflect society's general need for economic growth.

senses.definition: To fix the course of; to impel and direct; with a remoter object preceded by to.
examples: The news of his father's illness determined him to depart immediately.

senses.definition: To bring to a conclusion, as a question or controversy; to settle authoritative or judicial sentence; to decide.
examples: The court has determined the cause.

senses.definition: To resolve (to do something); to establish a fixed intention; to cause (something) to come to a conclusion or decision; to lead.
examples: I determined to go home at once.

senses.definition: (logic) To define or limit by adding a differentia.
(transitive or intransitive, law, otherwise obsolete) To bring to an end, finish; to come to an end, stop, end.
